Extract the grafting information from grafted phylogenies

Source: R/extract_grafting_info.R
extract_grafting_info.Rd

Summarize, in a table, where and when each grafted taxon (or missing clade) was grafted on the backbone: the age of the graft, the backbone branch it was grafted on (the parent clade), and, with a simmap, the state at the graft point and the state inherited by the grafted lineage. The function works a posteriori, on the output of phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa() or phylograftR::graft_missing_clades() (a phylogeny, a set of simulations, or the list of maps obtained with a "multiSimmap").

The table is meant to check the plausibility of the grafting against the backbone, and, over a set of phylogenies, to describe the uncertainty of the grafting (e.g., the distribution of the graft ages and graft states of each taxon).

Usage

extract_grafting_info(phy_grafted, missing_taxa_list, phy_backbone = NULL)

Arguments

phy_grafted

A grafted phylogeny (class "phylo"), a set of grafted phylogenies (class "multiPhylo", e.g., several simulations), or a list of them with one element per map (output of the grafting functions with a "multiSimmap").

missing_taxa_list

The list of missing taxa used for the grafting. Items: $Taxon_name, and $Target_clade (taxa, grafted with phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa()) or $Sister_clade (missing clades, grafted with phylograftR::graft_missing_clades()). Exactly one of them must be provided per list.

Alternatively, you can provide the list of both types of missing lineages taxa as list(taxa = ..., clades = ...), as returned by phylograftR::build_missing_taxa_list() when both types are provided (e.g., to use with phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa_and_clades()). The output is then a named list (see 'Value').

phy_backbone

Optional. The backbone phylogeny used for the grafting (class "phylo"). If NULL (default), the backbone is rebuilt by removing the grafted taxa from the grafted phylogeny (same topology and branch lengths): the taxa of missing_taxa_list (both types if a list(taxa, clades) is provided), and the tips flagged in $grafted_tips. The node IDs of the backbone (parent_node) can only be reported if phy_backbone is provided.

Value

A data.frame, with one row per taxon (or per missing clade) and phylogeny.

With a list(taxa, clades) covering both types of missing lineages, the output is a named list with the elements taxa and clades, each data.frame containing the output of its type (as described below).

The columns are:

  • map Character string. Name of the stochastic map (NA if no map was used).

  • simulation Integer. Index of the simulation.

  • seed Integer. Seed of the simulation (NA if unknown).

For missing taxa:

  • Taxon_name Character string. Name of the taxon.

  • parent_node Integer. Node ID in phy_backbone of the tipward end of the backbone branch of the graft point (NA without phy_backbone).

  • parent_tips Character string. Tips defining the parent clade.

  • graft_age Numeric. Age of the graft point.

  • divergence_age Numeric. Age of the node where the taxon splits from its sister lineage.

  • grafted_on Character string. Taxa grafted on the sister lineage (first five), NA if the taxon is attached directly to the backbone.

For missing clades:

  • Missing_clade Integer. Clade ID.

  • Taxa Character string. Taxa of the missing clade, separated by commas.

  • n_taxa Integer. Number of taxa in the grafted clade.

  • parent_node Integer. Node ID in phy_backbone of the tipward end of the backbone branch of the graft point (NA without phy_backbone).

  • parent_tips Character string. Tips defining the parent clade.

  • graft_age Numeric. Age of the graft point = stem age of the grafted clade.

  • crown_age Numeric. Crown age of the grafted clade.

With a simmap: parent_state and tip_state (taxa) or clade_state (missing clades), or one column per trait.

Attributes: "type" ("taxa" or "clades").

Details

What is extracted depends on the type of grafting

Missing taxa ($Target_clade list): one row per taxon. A taxon can be grafted on a branch of the backbone, or on a branch of a taxon grafted before it (and so on): the grafted taxa that hang together form a grafted subtree attached to the backbone at a graft point. The summary table reports:

  • graft_age: the age of the graft point, where the grafted subtree is attached to a branch of the backbone;

  • divergence_age: the age of the node where the taxon splits from its sister lineage. It is equal to graft_age for a taxon attached directly to the backbone, and younger for a taxon attached to another grafted taxon (grafted_on then lists the grafted taxa of its sister lineage).

  • The parent clade is the clade of the backbone subtended by the branch of the graft point: parent_tips gives two tips defining it (one if the branch is terminal), and parent_node its node ID in phy_backbone.

Missing clades ($Sister_clade list): one row per missing clade (the taxa with the same sister clade, grafted together). The missing clade is attached to the stem branch of its sister clade at a graft point. The summary table reports:

  • graft_age: the age of the graft point;

  • crown_age: the age of the most recent common ancestor of the taxa of the clade (NA for a single taxon);

  • The parent clade is the backbone clade subtended by the branch it was attached to (the sister clade, if the constraints were respected, see phylograftR::check_grafting_constraints()). If the taxa of a missing clade do not form a clade in the phylogeny, the values of the row are NA, with a warning.

States

If the phylogeny has a $simmap (output of the grafting with a simmap and return_simmap = TRUE), the states are extracted: parent_state is the state of the branch of the backbone at the graft point, and tip_state (taxa) or clade_state (missing clades) the state inherited by the grafted lineage.

They are different if treat_states_as_ranges = TRUE: a taxon grafted on a branch in the range "AB" can inherit the range "A". With the maps of several traits ($simmap is a list), there is one column per trait (parent_state_<trait>, tip_state_<trait>). The states are NA for phylogenies without $simmap, or whose $simmap does not match the phylogeny (e.g., after removing tips).

See also

Other functions from phylograftR:

  • phylograftR::check_grafting_plan() to check a priori the feasibility of a grafting plan, before grafting.

  • phylograftR::check_grafting_constraints() to check a posteriori that grafted taxa respect their constraints.

  • phylograftR::extract_sampling_info() to extract the richness and the sampling fraction of the clades in each grafted phylogeny.

  • phylograftR::extract_BD_model_summary() to extract a posteriori information on the birth-death models fitted during grafting.

  • phylograftR::identify_grafted() to identify the grafted tips and branches of a phylogeny.

Author

Maël Doré

Examples

# --- Prepare data --- #

# Create a toy backbone phylogeny: ultrametric, with a root age of 50 time units
set.seed(1234)
phy <- ape::rcoal(n = 30)
phy$edge.length <- phy$edge.length / max(ape::node.depth.edgelength(phy)) * 50

# List the missing taxa to graft
missing_taxa_list <- list(
  Taxon_name = c("X1", "X2", "X3", "X4"),
  Target_clade = list(X1 = c("t26", "t18"), X2 = c("t8", "t22"), X3 = "t5", X4 = c("t26", "t18")))

# --- Graft the taxa (several simulations) --- #

grafted_phy <- graft_missing_taxa(phy = phy, missing_taxa_list = missing_taxa_list,
                                  nb_simulations = 5, verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234)

# --- Extract the grafting information --- #

info <- extract_grafting_info(phy_grafted = grafted_phy, missing_taxa_list = missing_taxa_list,
                              phy_backbone = phy)
head(info)
#>    map simulation      seed Taxon_name parent_node parent_tips  graft_age
#> 1 <NA>          1      1234         X1          52     t6, t20 0.74762887
#> 2 <NA>          1      1234         X2          30         t22 1.85178529
#> 3 <NA>          1      1234         X3          27          t5 0.00441298
#> 4 <NA>          1      1234         X4           9         t28 2.95133160
#> 5 <NA>          2 488349520         X1          15         t24 0.53229148
#> 6 <NA>          2 488349520         X2          59    t13, t17 0.38557333
#>   divergence_age grafted_on
#> 1     0.74762887       <NA>
#> 2     1.85178529       <NA>
#> 3     0.00441298       <NA>
#> 4     2.95133160       <NA>
#> 5     0.53229148       <NA>
#> 6     0.38557333       <NA>

# Inspect uncertainty of the graft age of each taxon over the simulations
# Average minimum and maximum graft age across simulations
aggregate(graft_age ~ Taxon_name, data = info, FUN = function (x) round(range(x), 1))
#>   Taxon_name graft_age.1 graft_age.2
#> 1         X1         0.5         4.3
#> 2         X2         0.1         2.4
#> 3         X3         0.0         0.6
#> 4         X4         0.4         3.0

# --- Both types of missing lineages, grafted in one run --- #

# With list(taxa, clades), the information is extracted for each type, with the same backbone
both_list <- list(
  taxa = missing_taxa_list,
  clades = list(Taxon_name = c("M1", "M2"), Sister_clade = list(M1 = c("t8", "t22"), M2 = "t5")))
grafted_both <- graft_missing_taxa_and_clades(phy = phy, missing_taxa_list = both_list,
                                              nb_simulations = 3, verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234)
info_both <- extract_grafting_info(phy_grafted = grafted_both, missing_taxa_list = both_list,
                                   phy_backbone = phy)
names(info_both)
#> [1] "taxa"   "clades"
head(info_both$clades)
#>    map simulation      seed Missing_clade Taxa n_taxa parent_node parent_tips
#> 1 <NA>          1      1234             1   M1      1          33      t8, t5
#> 2 <NA>          1      1234             2   M2      1          27          t5
#> 3 <NA>          2 488349520             1   M1      1          33      t8, t5
#> 4 <NA>          2 488349520             2   M2      1          27          t5
#> 5 <NA>          3 469344150             1   M1      1          33      t8, t5
#> 6 <NA>          3 469344150             2   M2      1          27          t5
#>      graft_age crown_age
#> 1 27.886880636        NA
#> 2  0.002746001        NA
#> 3 19.135357456        NA
#> 4  0.075010203        NA
#> 5 38.930312846        NA
#> 6  0.099970264        NA
